regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8%; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% is the headline; the quality test is harder to pass. IIP overall at 6.7% — down from 8.8% — while capital goods at 16.1% and capacity utilisation at 77.4% (up 180bps) suggest the investment side is carrying growth that consumption hasn't yet fully validated. PMI composite at 54.6 is encouraging, but manufacturing PMI slipped to 52.8 from 53.5 — the services sector is doing the heavy lifting, and services-led growth at this stage of the cycle tends to be less employment-generative in the informal economy where 85% of workers sit.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45%; Fuel 22.93%","signal_text":"CPI at 4.45% masks a dangerous internal split: core CPI at 3.9% (28th percentile, genuinely subdued) while fuel inflation at 22.93% sits at a 10-year high — the 95th percentile. This divergence is the RBI's trap: core gives it cover to hold, but fuel at these levels feeds into transport costs, logistics margins, and eventually food prices with a 2-quarter lag. WPI at 9.92% rising alongside fuel means producer margins are being squeezed — either they absorb it (earnings risk) or they pass it through (CPI risk in Q1 FY28).","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1%; CD 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% — a 630bps divergence — with the CD ratio at 81.4% (75th percentile) is the structural fault line of this cycle. NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% from 10.6% signals that as banks tighten deposit competition, NBFCs are filling the gap via wholesale funding — precisely the channel that seized in 2018. Credit card growth at 2.3% (down from 5.6%) suggests the regulator's risk-weight tightening on unsecured lending is already biting at the margin; the question is whether that restraint spreads to secured categories before deposit growth catches up.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25%","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% with RBI's own inflation forecast revised up 50bps to 5.1% leaves a real rate of approximately 15bps — thin enough to be irrelevant as an anchor. With INR at 96.15 (91st percentile) and fuel inflation at a decade high, the RBI is not cutting; but it cannot hike without choking a capex cycle that capacity utilisation data says is just beginning. Extended pause is the only viable stance, but every month of pause with credit growing at 17% and deposits at 10.8% is a month the banking system's structural vulnerability deepens.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1%; CU 77.4%","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY with capacity utilisation at 77.4% — the threshold above which private capex historically accelerates in India — is the most genuinely encouraging data point in today's set. Core sector at 5.4% (moderating from 6%) is the caveat: cement and steel dispatch, the ground-level proxies for actual construction activity, are decelerating even as the headline investment numbers look strong. Manufacturing PMI at 52.8 (down from 53.5) confirms order book stability without overheating — a Goldilocks setup for capex, provided the credit channel doesn't tighten before private investment fully takes the baton from public capex.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST 199853; PV 16%","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 Cr is a strong print — but at the 71st percentile, not a record, and the YTD figure at the 14th percentile suggests the base is doing significant work. Passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY and two-wheeler at 19.7% are the more reliable demand signals: two-wheeler growth above PV growth indicates rural and semi-urban demand is participating, not just the top decile. The inversion worth watching: credit card growth at 2.3% (26th percentile) while PV sales run at 16% — either consumers are funding durables from savings and income rather than revolving credit (healthy), or the unsecured credit tightening is already constraining a segment of demand that the vehicle numbers haven't yet reflected.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (Mar 2026) vs deposit growth at 10.8% — a 350bps divergence widening for three consecutive months. CD ratio at 81.4% (down from 82.5% prior month but structurally elevated). NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY, signalling wholesale funding pressure as banks tighten retail deposit competition.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios >45% — they'll poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities; margin compression and refinancing risk are acute. RBI will likely signal liquidity support (OMOs, CRR cuts) within 6-8 weeks if deposit growth doesn't accelerate. Position for rate cuts in H2 2026.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile historically precedes either deposit acceleration or credit slowdown. Last time we saw this divergence (2022), RBI cut rates 250bps within 9 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capacity Utilisation Signals Sustained Investment","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY with capacity utilisation at 77.4% (up 180bps from 75.6% prior month). Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY, moderating but still positive. Manufacturing PMI at 52.8 (down from 53.5) signals order book stability without overheating.","implication":"Capex cycle is self-sustaining — 77.4% utilisation is the sweet spot where corporates invest without fear of stranded assets. Overweight capital goods, cement, and steel. Domestic equipment makers (Cummins, Kirloskar, Escorts) will see order acceleration. Public sector capex remains the anchor; private capex is now following. Expect 12-15% IIP capgoods growth to persist through FY27.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 74th percentile has historically preceded 18-24 months of sustained capex. This is mid-cycle, not late-cycle.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"Affluent Money Entering Via SIP Accounts","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,297 Cr (rising 2 consecutive months: 29,845→31,961→32,297). SIP accounts at 100.18 Cr (92nd percentile, 10-year high). But SIP AUM at ₹18.62 Tr (93rd percentile) growing faster than accounts — average ticket size rising sharply. MF AUM at ₹87.08 Tr (86th percentile), up 2 consecutive months. DII equity net at ₹58,502 Cr (100th percentile, all-time high).","implication":"This is NOT mass retail SIP — this is affluent/HNI money entering via systematic routes. Average SIP ticket is now ₹18.6 Lakh, up from ₹16.4 Lakh six months ago. This is late-cycle behaviour: wealthy investors hedging inflation via equity. Overweight large-cap quality (Nifty 50 constituents with >20% ROE). Avoid micro/small-cap — they'll underperform when this cohort rotates. Watch for SIP growth deceleration as a leading indicator of market peak.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP accounts at 92nd percentile with AUM at 93rd percentile is a rare combination — last seen in late 2021 before the 2022 correction. Affluent inflows are sticky but sentiment-sensitive.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI's Comfort","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (up from 20.05% prior month, 95th percentile, 10-year high). WPI at 9.92% (up from 9.78%), core CPI at 3.9% (28th percentile, low). Brent crude at $97.81/bbl (69th percentile, mid-range). Natural gas at $3.17/MMBtu (up from $2.83, 20th percentile but rising sharply).","implication":"Fuel inflation is the tail risk to RBI's 4% CPI target. If Brent breaches $105/bbl (geopolitical shock), headline CPI could spike to 5.5%+ within 2 months, forcing RBI to pause/hike despite deposit stress. Hedge via long crude positions or energy stocks (ONGC, Reliance). Avoid rate-sensitive sectors (auto, cement) until fuel inflation moderates below 15%. Monitor Middle East tensions and OPEC+ production cuts closely.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is a structural shock, not cyclical. Last time fuel inflation was this high (2022), RBI hiked 250bps despite growth concerns.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"watch","title":"BOJ Tightening Unwinds Yen Carry Trades","data_text":"BOJ rate at 1.0% (up from 0.75%, 86th percentile, 10-year high). Fed funds at 3.63% (flat, 67th percentile). US 10Y Treasury at 4.96% (90th percentile, near highs). DXY at 101.11 (flat, 53rd percentile). INR/USD at 96.15 (up from 95.69, 91st percentile, 10-year high). US PMI composite at 56.0 (84th percentile), EU PMI at 53.5 (82nd percentile).","implication":"BOJ's rate hike is unwinding the yen carry trade — this is a structural headwind for emerging market liquidity. INR weakness (96.15) is a symptom, not the disease. FII flows will remain volatile; expect 2-3 weeks of outflows if US yields stay >5.0%. RBI will likely intervene to defend 95.50 on INR/USD. Reduce EM currency exposure; overweight INR hedges (long USD calls). Watch for a BOJ pause signal in April — that's the inflection point for EM re-rating.","pct_10y":86,"pct_note":"BOJ at 86th percentile with US 10Y at 90th percentile is a rare policy divergence. Last time this happened (2015), EM currencies fell 15-20% before stabilising.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakness Signals RBI Intervention Limits","data_text":"INR/USD at 96.15 (up from 95.69, 91st percentile, 10-year high). FII equity net at ₹29,631 Cr (up from -₹3,111.9 Cr prior month, 83rd percentile). Recent trend: -114→-3,111.9→+29,631 (volatile, 1 of last 2 up). India VIX at 10.345 (down from 11.25, 5th percentile, 10-year low — complacency signal).","implication":"INR at 96.15 is a warning shot. RBI has likely burned $3-5 Bn in reserves defending 95.50 in the past 6 weeks. If BOJ stays hawkish and US yields stay >5.0%, INR could test 97.0 within 4 weeks. This will force RBI to either (a) hike rates (conflicting with deposit stress), or (b) accept depreciation (inflation pass-through). Overweight INR hedges; reduce long USD exposure in emerging market baskets. India VIX at 5th percentile is dangerous — volatility will spike when INR breaks 96.50.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"INR at 91st percentile weakness with VIX at 5th percentile complacency is a classic divergence. Last time this occurred (Aug 2022), INR fell another 4% before stabilising.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Decoupling From IT Stock Proxy","data_text":"Office absorption at 24.6 Mn sqft (up from 20.8 Mn sqft, 18th percentile, 10-year low). Office vacancy at 14.5% (down from 16.1%, 42nd percentile). Nifty IT index flat YTD while office absorption rising. GCC (Global Capability Centre) leasing now 35-40% of total office demand vs 15% five years ago. Rent growth in Bengaluru at 100.6 (up from 94, 57th percentile) and Mumbai at 125 (up from 117.9, 38th percentile).","implication":"Traditional IT services (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) are NOT the marginal office buyer anymore — GCCs (captive centres of MNCs like Apple, Google, Amazon) are. This means office RE is decoupling from IT stock valuations. Overweight commercial real estate (Embassy, Mindspace) and underweight IT services on valuation. GCC expansion is sticky (5-10 year leases) vs IT services (cyclical). The office market is healthier than IT stock prices suggest — this is a 12-month alpha opportunity. Falsifiable: if GCC leasing falls below 30% of total demand, thesis breaks.","pct_10y":18,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 18th percentile looks weak in isolation, but the composition shift (GCC dominance) is structurally bullish for landlords. This is a hidden strength masked by headline weakness.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP growth with PMI composite at 54.6 looks like a clean expansion — until you separate the engines. Capital goods IIP at 16.1% and capacity utilisation at 77.4% confirm a genuine investment upcycle; but IIP overall at 6.7% (down from 8.8%) and core sector at 5.4% (down from 6%) signal that the broader industrial base is not accelerating in lockstep. Fuel inflation at 22.93% — a 10-year high — is the variable that can unravel the narrative fastest: every sustained quarter at these levels compresses rural disposable income, and two-wheeler sales at 19.7%, while strong today, are the first indicator to watch for demand fatigue. RBI's own growth forecast at 6.7% sits 110bps below the current print — the gap between what the central bank believes is sustainable and what the data currently shows is itself a signal worth holding.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US PMI composite at 56.0 (84th percentile) and Euro Stoxx 50 at a 100th-percentile 6,299 — even after today's marginal pullback — describe a global economy that is re-accelerating, which is precisely the wrong backdrop for central banks trying to declare victory on inflation. US 10Y at 4.96% (90th percentile) with Fed funds flat at 3.63% means the bond market is doing the Fed's tightening for it — but US GDP SAAR at 1.5% (down from 2.1%) says the real economy is already feeling it. BOJ at 1.0% (86th percentile, up from 0.75%) is the underappreciated global variable: yen carry unwind at this pace historically correlates with EM volatility within 60-90 days, and India's INR at 96.15 is already at the 91st percentile. China at 4.3% GDP (down from 5.0%) with composite PMI at 49.5 — below 50 — is the demand drag that prevents any commodity-led global reflation from becoming self-sustaining.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

DII equity net at ₹58,502 Cr — a 100th-percentile all-time high, rising for two consecutive months — is the most consequential liquidity fact of the week, and it is being driven by SIP inflows at ₹32,297 Cr (92nd percentile) where AUM at ₹18.62 Tr is growing faster than account additions — average ticket size is rising, meaning affluent savers are increasing allocation, not just new participants entering. FII equity net swung to ₹29,631 Cr positive from -₹3,112 Cr prior month, but the trend is volatile (1 of last 2 months positive) — this is not a structural FII return, it is a positioning adjustment. The risk embedded in this liquidity picture: India VIX at 10.345 (5th percentile, falling for five consecutive sessions) signals a market pricing near-zero tail risk precisely when BOJ tightening, INR at decade highs, and fuel inflation at decade highs are all live variables — complacency at this level has historically preceded sharp, fast corrections rather than gradual ones.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Nifty 50 at 23,447 (75th percentile) and Bank Nifty at 56,549 (93rd percentile) are pricing a credit cycle that the deposit data does not yet support — Bank Nifty at the 93rd percentile while CD ratio sits at 81.4% and deposit growth trails credit by 630bps is a divergence that resolves either through NIM compression or macro-prudential tightening, neither of which is in current consensus earnings. Office absorption at 24.6 Mn sqft rising 18% sequentially tells a structurally different story from listed REIT prices: Embassy, Mindspace, and Brookfield REITs are down 15-25% from prior levels even as GCC leasing — now 35-40% of total office demand versus 15% five years ago — is structurally repricing the demand base. Residential real estate shows unsold inventory at 6,16,000 units (62nd percentile, rising) alongside declining sales units — affordability at the 19th percentile with home loan rates averaging 7.55% is the binding constraint, and any further INR weakness feeding into imported inflation will delay the rate relief that housing demand is waiting for.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three risks, ranked by probability × impact. First: fuel inflation at 22.93% with Brent at $97.81 — if Brent crosses $100 and sustains, every $10 adds approximately $15bn to India's import bill, widens CAD by 40bps, and puts the RBI in the position of defending INR with reserves rather than rate policy, since hiking into a slowing IIP is not viable. Second: BOJ at 1.0% unwinding yen carry — the historical window for EM stress after a BOJ hike of this magnitude is 60-90 days; India's FX reserves provide a buffer, but INR at the 91st percentile with VIX at the 5th percentile means the market is not priced for the test. Third: bank credit at 17.1% against deposit growth of 10.8% — if NBFC wholesale funding costs rise as the carry unwind pressures domestic rates, the credit channel tightens precisely when the capex cycle needs it most open. Watch US 10Y — a sustained break above 5.0% this week is the single data point that tightens all three risks simultaneously.

"}
